title: H288: LLM-Constrained Factor Discovery via DSL Audit Trail
rationale: arXiv:2604.26747 'From Hypotheses to Factors: Constrained LLM Agents in Cryptocurrency Markets' achieves OOS Sharpe 1.55, 44.55% annualized return (2024-2026 OOS, 5bp one-way costs) using a constrained LLM factor search with a point-in-time factor DSL. The key methodological innovation is CONSTRAINING LLM flexibility: candidate factor expressions are restricted to a domain-specific language (DSL) that enforces fixed data splits, selection gates, transaction costs, and portfolio tests — preventing uncontrolled alpha mining. This directly addresses Kevin's concern about overfitting in H-series LLM hypothesis generation. Design for US equities: (1) Define a DSL of allowable factor expressions over OHLCV + fundamentals (e.g., 'rank(momentum_Nd / std_Nd)', 'rank(FCF/P) - rank(momentum_6m)'); (2) Use Claude/GPT-4o-mini to propose 20-30 factor expressions in DSL syntax; (3) Auto-test each against H217 IS/OOS framework (IS 2008-2017, OOS 2018-2025); (4) Ridge-combine surviving factors into a composite; (5) Gate: composite OOS Sharpe > 1.3 (vs H217 baseline 1.559 — slightly below since combining may dilute). Use S&P 500 30-stock universe with survivorship-bias caveat. Script implements the DSL parser + LLM proposal loop + auto-backtest runner.

# H288: LLM-Constrained Factor Discovery (arXiv:2604.26747)
# Constrained DSL approach to prevent uncontrolled alpha mining
# OOS Sharpe 1.55 on crypto; adapting to US equity 30-stock universe
# IS: 2008-2017, OOS: 2018-2025
# Gate: ridge-combined factor composite OOS Sharpe > 1.3
#
# DSL factor primitives (allowed operations):
# - rank(x)              : cross-sectional rank [0,1]
# - momentum(n)          : n-day price return (price_n / price_0 - 1)
# - std(x, n)            : rolling n-day std of daily returns
# - rank(x) - rank(y)    : composite ranking
# - ts_rank(x, n)        : time-series rank of x over n periods
# - corr(x, y, n)        : rolling n-day correlation
# - NOT allowed: look-ahead (future data), survivor-selected universes, resampled returns
#
# LLM proposal prompt:
# 'Given this DSL, propose 5 factor expressions for cross-sectional stock selection.
#  Each expression must be a valid combination of DSL primitives.
#  Express as Python lambda over df columns: close, volume, returns_1d,...
#  Reason step by step. Output JSON list of {name, expression, economic_rationale}'
#
# TODO: implement DSL parser
# TODO: implement LLM proposal loop (3 rounds x 7 proposals = 21 candidates)
# TODO: auto-backtest each candidate against H217 framework
